answer: After the harvest the pits are counted on the board and the orchard elder checks the count against the palms he walked himself. A jade pit bought from another orchard fails the board: at the terrace of the count the pits must match the harvest the elder saw, and bought pits are the wrong size. Forging a count means tending palms for three years, bribing an elder and paying 15,600, while the sparrow tally on the board is kept in the oasis storehouse, so a harvest whose pits were never counted is left to rot.
